transcript:
Date: 2025-10-09 | Start: 11:00 AM PST | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood CSM), Maya (Acme CISO), Liam (Acme Head Infra), Sara (App Sec), Dmitri (Compliance)

Summary: Quick review of the recent Redwood penetration test, discussion of a handful of medium/critical findings, vulnerability management cadence, and questions about SOC 2/ISO evidence, RBAC, SSO integration, KMS and data residency options. Agreed next steps and remediation timelines.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 45 minutes, quick agenda — pen test highlights, remediation, vuln mgmt, patch cadence, then Q&A.
00:12 Maya: Morning, thanks. We got the spreadsheet, nice to see details; we're most worried about the criticals flagged around the admin console and container runtime.
00:28 Priya: Yep, we ran the pentest last month, redacted report attached. There were three findings we marked critical, two high, a handful medium. We'll go through them one by one.
00:44 Sara: Just a note, Acme has a 7-day SLA for critical fixes in prod, 30-day for high. Need to understand Redwood's patch cadence for managed infra.
01:05 Priya: For hosted API we push security patches to control plane within 24-72 hours for critical CVEs, for customer-dedicated pools we coordinate windows — typical patch cadence monthly for noncritical, emergency for critical. If you're in Dedicated we can do scheduled maintenance with advance notice.
01:29 Liam: When you say control plane, do you mean Redwood-managed? Our requirement for private deployment is we want the control plane in VPC and we manage patching. Can you clarify responsibilities?
01:44 Priya: Right — for Redwood Private the customer controls the host patching unless you opt into Redwood managed services. For Dedicated it's a shared responsibility, Redwood patches runtime and orchestrator kernels, customers handle app layer unless we have a support contract.
02:05 Dmitri: On SOC 2/ISO evidence, can you share the latest Type II report and scope? We need to validate log retention and audit trails for our auditors.
02:18 Jordan: Absolutely, I'll drop the SOC 2 Type II link and the ISO 27001 certificate — Priya will include a mapping of audit log retention and where S3 logs land in our hosted offering.
02:32 Priya: For audit logs, hosted keeps audit trails for 90 days by default, with extended retention as an add-on. For Private deployments logs stay in your environment and we surface the same events.
02:48 Sara: Does your audit log capture token-level access and model call metadata? We need per-user tracing for compliance.
03:02 Priya: Yes, we capture token-level call events: request metadata, route, model, user id where provided, and error traces. Might be gaps in auto-inferred identifiers if you're using anon keys — that's expected.
03:18 Maya: Encryption — are keys customer-managed? We need KMS/HSM integration and want to ensure keys never leave our KMS.
03:30 Priya: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS/HSM. For Private deployments it's straightforward; for hosted we support envelope encryption and can BYOK for enterprise plans. Keys are used for data at rest encryption but transactional KV cache encryption is a separate path — we'll follow up with crypto team notes.
03:56 Liam: About the pentest specifics — one of the critical findings references container escape potential in an older runtime and an example CVE listed. Was that in your managed image or a third-party dependency?
04:12 Priya: That was in a third-party dependency in the inference runtime we use for a legacy model path; patch has been applied in hosted and Dedicated control planes last week. For Private installs we provided a hotfix and we recommend customers run the updated runtime.
04:32 Sara: Our AppSec team wants repro steps and timeline to validate.
04:40 Priya: We'll provide repro steps redacted, and a timeline: discovery 2025-09-12, exploit validation 2025-09-18, fix rolled 2025-10-01 in hosted.
04:56 Sara: Good. For verification, will you run a scan against our Dedicated pool after we apply updates?
05:06 Jordan: Yes, we can schedule a collaborative retest with our engineering team. We'll need a window and access method you prefer.
05:20 Dmitri: On vulnerability management, what's your triage and patching cadence for dependencies? Do you run weekly vulnerability scans?
05:33 Priya: We run automated dependency scans daily across our base images and runtime components, weekly SCA reports are generated, critical alerts route to on-call. We maintain an internal backlog and SLA: criticals triaged within 24h, remediation planning in 72h.
05:52 Maya: How do you handle third-party model weights and supply chain risk? Some of our teams insist on reproducible provenance and checksums.
06:06 Priya: We maintain a model catalog with provenance metadata and checksums. For open weights we validate hashes and can provide a SBOM-like manifest for runtime libs. For private model onboarding we run an intake review and quarantined validation.
06:26 Sara: Secure SDLC — do you require static analysis and threat modeling for code that touches customer data?
06:34 Priya: Yes, our SDLC includes SAST for service code, DAST on public endpoints, dependency scanning, and periodic threat modeling for major features. We also use automated gating in CI for high-severity findings.
06:52 Liam: Patching cadence question again — if a critical kernel CVE appears, what's the rollback plan if a patch breaks inference performance?
07:07 Priya: We maintain canary and gradual rollout with performance telemetry. If a patch causes regressions we have automatic fallback to previous runtime and can route traffic to a compatible model variant while fix is applied. For Dedicated we coordinate with your infra team for rollback windows.
07:29 Maya: Anything flagged around RBAC or SSO in the pen test?
07:36 Priya: There was a medium finding where an old role mapping allowed broader access than intended in a test account; remediation is rule tightening and adding least-privilege checks. We've updated default role templates and recommend you review your SAML assertions mapping.
07:58 Sara: Do you support SCIM for provisioning to reduce stale accounts?
08:04 Priya: Yes, SCIM + SAML SSO supported for enterprise. We can enable JIT provisioning and deprovisioning hooks.
08:16 Dmitri: Data residency — our auditors require that logs and customer data for EU customers remain in EU. How's that handled?
08:26 Priya: We have regionally isolated deployments, and we can deploy private control plane in a region to meet residency. Hosted accounts can be pinned to EU region and we assure data residency for stored artifacts.
08:40 Jordan: Quick callout — encryption in transit is TLS 1.2+ with options to enforce 1.3; at rest uses AES-256 with CMKs for enterprise.
08:53 Liam: On evidence for auditors, can you provide past pen test attestations and patch timelines?
09:00 Jordan: We'll bundle the redacted pentest report, patch timeline, SOC 2 Type II, ISO cert, and an audit log mapping doc.
09:12 Maya: About remediation acceptance — we need to run our validators and confirm in staging before sign-off. Is that ok?
09:20 Priya: Totally fine — we can coordinate a staging validation run and provide artifact hashes and repro steps.
09:31 Sara: Any outstanding criticals that aren't fixed yet?
09:35 Priya: One critical for an older dependency in a Private customer's install remains open until their team applies our hotfix; we flagged it with that customer for immediate action. For Acme's reported items, your Dedicated pools were already patched by our ops team on 2025-10-01 except the role-mapping which is config-only.
09:55 Maya: Good. For timelines — can you commit to remediation plans in writing? Auditors want dates.
10:03 Jordan: We'll provide a remediation plan doc with owners and dates — Priya will draft and share by 2025-10-16.
10:14 Dmitri: A few clarifying Qs on audit logs sampling — do you provide full request payloads or just metadata? Our policy is to avoid storing PII in logs.
10:26 Priya: By default we log metadata and identifiers; payloads are not persisted unless configured for debug and then redacted. For hosted we strip PII by default. We'll share the log schema.
10:40 Sara: Great. One last thing: what's your disclosure policy if a CVE affects hosted customers simultaneously? Do you have a customer notification cadence?
10:50 Priya: We have incident communication templates — initial notification within 2 hours for critical incidents, follow-ups with remediation status and postmortem. Dedicated/private customers also get direct Slack/phone escalation as part of their SLA.
11:05 Jordan: Ok, recap and next steps: Redwood will share redacted pen test report and SOC/ISO artifacts, Priya will draft remediation plan and patch schedule, Acme provides prioritized asset list and will schedule a staging validation window. We'll reconvene on 2025-10-16 for deep dive.
11:18 Maya: Thanks everyone.
11:21 Jordan: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
